title: Because, So and But
description: Join two sentences into one real thought: give the reason, the purpose and the consequence, and learn the Yemeni excuse that keeps everybody's face — the traffic, the circumstances, and معليش.
approach: GPA Phase 3 — the learner hears reasons and consequences in context, then builds their own excuse chain from cards before saying it.
unlock_condition: Give three reasons for being late using لأن, عشان and مع إن, each in a full sentence
can_do: Give a reason and a consequence
Join sentences with 'but', 'although' and 'in order to'
Make an excuse politely and accept one gracefully

grammar.title: Linking two sentences: لأن، حتى، عشان كذا، مع إن
grammar.explanation: لأن 'because' takes a whole sentence or a pronoun ending: لأني 'because I', لأنه 'because he / because it'. حتى + a present verb without بـ gives a purpose: جيت حتى أشوفك 'I came so that I'd see you'; عشان does the same job and also means 'because of' before a noun. To say 'that's why', put عشان كذا at the front of the result. مع إن 'although' introduces the surprising part and بس 'but' answers it: مع إن الطريق زحمة، بس وصلت بدري. Keep each half short — Yemeni speech chains small sentences rather than building long ones.

examples.english: I was late because the road was jammed
I went to the market in order to buy qat

examples.arabic: السيارة تعطلت، عشان كذا جيت بالتاكسي
examples.transliteration: is-sayyaara tʿaṭṭalat, ʿashaan kadha jiit bit-taksi
examples.english: The car broke down, that's why I came by taxi
Although I'm tired, I'll still come
I didn't come because of the circumstances

culture.title: The reason given is not always the reason
culture.note: In Yemen an excuse protects two faces at once: yours for failing and the other person's for having been let down. So the reason offered is often a soft one — الظروف 'circumstances', الزحمة 'the traffic', شغل 'work' — and the real reason stays private. Nobody investigates. The correct reply to an excuse is instant forgiveness: معليش 'never mind', عادي 'no big deal', الله يعينك 'God help you'. Add والله before your excuse to show you mean it, and اعذرني 'forgive me' if it was serious. What you must never do is demand the real reason.

phrases.english: Never mind, no big deal, God help you
Forgive me, I had an urgent errand

vocabulary.teaching_note: The main 'because' before a full sentence. With a pronoun it fuses: لأني، لأنك، لأنه، لأنها، لأنهم. Often typed لان online.
vocabulary.image_scene: Two speech bubbles linked by an arrow, the second labelled with a question mark turning into a tick.

example.english: I didn't go to work because I'm sick

vocabulary.video_hint: Anyone explaining themselves on camera; لأن right after a ليش question.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Before a present verb, حتى means 'in order to': حتى أشوفك 'so I can see you'. The verb after it takes no بـ. It also means 'even' and 'until' — the meaning shifts with what follows.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man holding a shopping bag with a thought bubble showing a cooked meal.

example.english: I came early so that I'd find a place

vocabulary.video_hint: Cooking and errand vlogs: 'I did X so that Y' with حتى / عشان.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The everyday 'therefore'. Literally 'because of this'. Sits at the start of the result. Never لذلك in speech — it sounds like a news bulletin.
vocabulary.image_scene: A flat tyre on the left, a man in a taxi on the right, an arrow between.

example.arabic: الجو حار، عشان كذا ما خرجناش
example.transliteration: ij-jaww ḥaarr, ʿashaan kadha maa kharajnaash
example.english: The weather is hot, that's why we didn't go out

vocabulary.video_hint: Explanations in vlogs; عشان كذا introducing the conclusion.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'Even though'. Fuses with pronouns like لأن: مع إني، مع إنه، مع إنها. The main clause often opens with بس.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man smiling under heavy rain with no umbrella.

example.arabic: مع إن السلتة حارة، بس أكلتها كلها
example.transliteration: maʿ inn is-salta ḥaarra, bass akaltaha kullaha
example.english: Although the saltah was spicy, I ate all of it

vocabulary.video_hint: Food reviews with a concession: 'although it was X, it was Y'.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'Even so, still'. Where English has 'however', a Yemeni speaker says مع هذا or just بس. Never مع ذلك — ذلك is not spoken here.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman shrugging with one hand up beside a closed shop sign, still smiling.

example.arabic: الدكان مسكّر، مع هذا لقينا خبز
example.transliteration: id-dukkaan msakkar, maʿ haadha ligiina khubz
example.english: The shop is closed; even so, we found bread

vocabulary.video_hint: Vloggers weighing pros and cons; مع هذا before the turn.

vocabulary.teaching_note: ايش السبب؟ 'what's the reason?'. بسبب + noun = 'because of': بسبب الزحمة. Plural أسباب.
vocabulary.image_scene: A question mark card and beneath it a magnifying glass over a clock.

example.english: What's the reason for the delay?

vocabulary.video_hint: Anyone asking ايش السبب؟ or explaining بسبب…

vocabulary.teaching_note: ذ is dh. عندك عذر 'you have an excuse' means you're forgiven; ما فيش عذر 'no excuse'. The verb اعذرني 'excuse me / forgive me' comes from the same root.
vocabulary.image_scene: A note card reading a doctor's slip handed across a desk.

example.arabic: هذا مش عذر، الشغل الساعة ثمان
example.transliteration: haadha mish ʿudhr, ish-shughl is-saaʿa thamaan
example.english: That's no excuse, work is at eight

vocabulary.video_hint: A boss or parent in a skit rejecting an excuse: مش عذر.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The all-purpose Yemeni excuse: الظروف 'the circumstances' covers money, health, family and the country at once. Singular ظرف. Pronounce ظ as an emphatic dh.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man spreading his hands helplessly in front of a dark house with a power cut.
vocabulary.video_hint: Everyday talk about hardship; الظروف as the reason for anything.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Both 'never mind' as forgiveness and 'sorry' as a soft apology. Also spelled معلش and ما عليش. Said fast, with a small wave of the hand.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman waving a hand dismissively with a warm smile at a friend who is apologising.
vocabulary.video_hint: Someone forgiving a small mishap on camera with معليش.

vocabulary.teaching_note: أنا متأخر 'I'm late', متأخرة for a woman. The verb is تأخّر 'to be late' — تأخرت 'I was late'. Hold the doubled kh.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man running with a bag, a large clock showing ten past the hour behind him.
vocabulary.video_hint: Someone rushing; متأخر / تأخرت in the voiceover.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Traffic jam or a crowd — the same word. الطريق زحمة 'the road is jammed', السوق زحمة 'the market is packed'. The number one excuse in Sanaa.
vocabulary.image_scene: A Sanaa street packed with cars and motorbikes, horns, a minaret behind.
vocabulary.video_hint: Driving vlogs in Sanaa; زحمة said while stuck at a roundabout.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Before an excuse it means 'honestly'; on its own with rising tone it means 'really?'. The ل is thick and dark: waɫɫa. Used constantly, so it carries little weight — والله العظيم is the strong form.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man with a hand on his chest, sincere face, speaking to a friend.

example.english: Honestly, I didn't know about the appointment

vocabulary.video_hint: Everywhere; والله opening an explanation or answering a doubt.

vocabulary.teaching_note: عندي موعد 'I have an appointment' — with a doctor, a landlord or a friend. Plural مواعيد. Being late to one needs an excuse.
vocabulary.image_scene: A calendar page with a time written and circled, a pen beside it.

example.arabic: عندي موعد مع الدكتور الساعة عشر
example.transliteration: ʿindi mawʿid maʿ id-duktoor is-saaʿa ʿashir
example.english: I have an appointment with the doctor at ten

vocabulary.video_hint: Phone calls fixing a time; موعد said with the hour.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The verb behind متأخر. تأخرت 'I was late', تأخر الباص 'the bus was delayed'. Pair with لأن for the classic excuse.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man arriving through a door to an empty meeting room, chairs pushed back.

example.english: I was late because the bus didn't come

vocabulary.video_hint: Skits about lateness; تأخرت with the excuse that follows.

vocabulary.teaching_note: For cars, phones and the electricity: السيارة تعطلت 'the car broke down', النت متعطل 'the internet is down'. A very respectable excuse.
vocabulary.image_scene: A car with its bonnet up on a mountain road, steam rising, a man on the phone.

example.english: The car broke down on the way

vocabulary.video_hint: Roadside breakdown moments in travel vlogs; تعطلت audible.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The word that ends an apology: عادي 'it's fine'. Also 'ordinary': يوم عادي 'an ordinary day'. Said with a shrug.
vocabulary.image_scene: A shrug emoji-style pose by a young man, palms up, relaxed face.
vocabulary.video_hint: Replies to apologies in sketches; عادي with a shrug.

vocabulary.teaching_note: An outing with a purpose: عندي مشوار 'I've got an errand to run'. Vague enough to be the perfect excuse.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man on a motorbike with a bag, a shop and a bank in the background.

example.english: I've got an errand this afternoon

vocabulary.video_hint: Daily vlogs announcing the day's مشوار before leaving the house.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The serious apology, from the same root as عذر. To a woman اعذريني, to a group اعذروني. Stronger than معليش; use it when you actually let someone down.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man with a hand over his heart and a slight bow toward an older man.

example.arabic: اعذرني يا عمي، ما قدرتش أجي
example.transliteration: iʿdhirni ya ʿammi, maa gidirtsh aji
example.english: Forgive me, uncle, I couldn't come

vocabulary.video_hint: Apologies in family scenes; اعذرني to an elder.

dialogue.speaker: Um Ahmed
dialogue.arabic: ليش تأخرت يا سالم؟ الغدا برد
dialogue.transliteration: leesh taʾakhkhart ya saalim? il-ghada birid
dialogue.english: Why are you late, Salem? Lunch has gone cold

dialogue.speaker: Salem
dialogue.arabic: اعذريني، والله الطريق كان زحمة قوي
dialogue.transliteration: iʿdhiriini, walla ṭ-ṭariig kaan zaḥma gawi
dialogue.english: Forgive me, honestly the road was really jammed

dialogue.speaker: Um Ahmed
dialogue.english: Jammed? It's two in the afternoon!

dialogue.speaker: Salem
dialogue.arabic: مع إني خرجت بدري، بس السيارة تعطلت، عشان كذا جيت بالتاكسي
dialogue.transliteration: maʿ inni kharajt badri, bass is-sayyaara tʿaṭṭalat, ʿashaan kadha jiit bit-taksi
dialogue.english: Although I left early, the car broke down, that's why I came by taxi

dialogue.speaker: Um Ahmed
dialogue.english: Never mind, it's fine. What was the reason for the breakdown?

dialogue.speaker: Salem
dialogue.arabic: ما أدري، الظروف. تعالي نتغدى حتى ما يبردش أكثر
dialogue.transliteration: maa adri, iẓ-ẓuruuf. taʿaali nitghadda ḥatta maa yibridsh akthar
dialogue.english: I don't know, circumstances. Come, let's eat so it doesn't get any colder

sound_spotlight.explanation: Both are dh sounds in Sanaa, but ظ is heavy — the tongue is pulled back and the vowel after it darkens. ẓuruuf sounds deeper than ʿudhr.
لأن glues onto its pronoun and the hamza almost vanishes: la-anni, la-annuh, la-annaha. Say it as one word with a doubled n.
The ل of الله is pronounced thick, at the back of the mouth, like the l in English 'full'. It is the most-heard word in any excuse.

lesson_sequence.detail: The learner hears the Salem dialogue once; the only task is to count the reasons he gives.
The five connectors on cards with two examples each and a colour: reason (لأن), purpose (حتى), result (عشان كذا), concession (مع إن / مع هذا).
The remaining words with images and example audio; the excuse nouns (سبب، عذر، ظروف، زحمة) grouped on one screen.
Drag cards to build an excuse: event + connector + reason. The app reads the result aloud and flags a mismatched connector.
Role-play with the AI: it makes an excuse and the learner replies with معليش / عادي; then the roles flip.
Record a three-sentence excuse for missing a lunch, using لأن, مع إن and عشان كذا.
Words-learned counter; culture nudge about never asking for the real reason.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Next time you are late, say اعذرني and give a reason with لأن — then notice how fast the other person says معليش.
real_world_prompts.context: Lesson-complete screen. Activates the apology and the forgiveness formula.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Explain to a friend why you chose your job or your city using عشان كذا.
real_world_prompts.context: Follow-up notification. Production of the result connector in a personal context.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Watch a Yemeni sketch about being late and list the excuses. Which was الظروف?
real_world_prompts.context: Video-companion prompt; recognition of excuse vocabulary.

video_needs.scene: A sketch where someone arrives late and explains; a driving vlog stuck in Sanaa traffic; a family scene with an excuse and its forgiving reply.
